- descriptive statistic

- cross tabulation

Hypothesis tests is divided into parametric test and non-parametric test

Parametric test or metric test deals with t test and z test

independent samples deals with two groups

Independent samples for non-parametric tests deals with chi-square, median, K-S

T test and Z test are identical if the sample size are the same for both

T test cover both small and big sample size

Z test only cover large same size

ANOVA is used for three or more groups

Two groups is reserved for T-test

Type of statistic can change based on nominal or ordinal scale

Chi-square is used in both independent sample and paired sample

Multivariate techniques is split into dependence and interdependence techniques

Dependence technique is where at least one independent variable can be identified

One dependent variable

- cross-tabulation

- analysis of variance and covariance

- multiple regression

More than one variable

- multivariate analysis of variance and covariance

- canonical correlation

- multiple discriminant analysis

Variable interdependence

- factor analysis

Interobject similarity

- cluster analysis

- multidimensional scaling
